title: Kickstart playground: micro-examples for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, and CLI with ergonomic streaming & retry patterns
creator: Anya Patel
description: Create a compact "kickstart" playground repo and example set that demonstrates idiomatic SDK usage across Next.js (TypeScript), FastAPI (Python), Go HTTP server, and a CLI tool. Focus on streaming ergonomics (client-side iterators, SSE/Fetch streaming, chunked responses), resilient retry patterns (idempotency keys, per-request backoff, jitter, retry budgets), and small cookbook snippets illustrating common production patterns (batching, prefix caching hints, graceful fallbacks to cheaper model variants). Each language should include a minimal app, one end-to-end integration test, and a README with copy-paste usage. Goal: reduce friction for engineers onboarding Redwood SDKs and provide canonical patterns for streaming + retries.
acceptance_criteria: Four minimal examples live in /examples: nextjs-ts, fastapi-py, go-http, cli-tool
Each example demonstrates streaming from the SDK and displays tokens progressively
Retry strategy documented and implemented (idempotency key, exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts configurable)
Readmes include copy-paste snippet, environment setup, and 'when to use' guidance
Automated e2e test per example that runs against local mock server and CI harness
Docs link added to developer quickstart and Console onboarding doc
tasks: Design API ergonomics for streaming responses (iterator + event callbacks) - proposal PR
Implement Next.js example: client uses Fetch streaming + SDK helper to map tokens to UI updates
Implement FastAPI example: backend proxy to Redwood SDK demonstrating async iteration + server-sent events endpoint
Implement Go example: net/http server presenting chunked responses with graceful reconnect semantics
CLI example: streaming output with resume token, progress spinner, and safe Ctrl-C handling
Add retry utilities in each example (idempotency header, retry budget, jittered backoff) and tests
Add CI job that spins mock inference runtime and runs e2e smoke tests
Write READMEs and small cookbook.md with 6 production tips (batching, cache hints, connection pooling, fallback models, request budgeting, observability hooks)
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff — scoped to minimal examples and cookbook guidance. Agreed to keep examples <200 LOC where possible.
2026-03-03: Prototype Next.js streaming UI using Fetch + ReadableStream — initial UX works but needs helper to normalize SDK events across browsers.
2026-03-05: FastAPI prototype uses async for await in SDK to relay SSE. Found an edge case when client cancels mid-stream; added server-side cleanup handler.
2026-03-07: Go chunked response prototype done. Observed high memory with naive buffer; switched to streaming encoder that flushes per token.
2026-03-08: CLI proof-of-concept shows resume token pattern (server sends final checkpoint). Need to harden idempotency header format.
2026-03-09: PM review (Sofia Ramos) — asked for clear 'when to use' sections and one benchmark comparing latency with/without local proxy. Added to tasks.
2026-03-10: Design feedback (Luca Moretti) — prefer compact TypeScript streaming helper that returns AsyncIterable<Event|Token> rather than callback API. Will refactor Next.js example.
2026-03-11: Security review quick-check — no secrets baked into examples; added note about KMS/HSM usage for Private customers in README.
2026-03-12: Code PRs opened: GH PR #1420 (nextjs streaming helper), #1423 (fastapi sse proxy), #1425 (go streaming server), #1426 (cli resume example). CI flakiness on Windows runner — investigating.
notes: Implementation choices: prefer AsyncIterable for language parity; keep each example idiomatic (TS uses ReadableStream/Fetch, Python uses async iterators & Starlette SSE, Go uses net/http chunking). Emphasize small helpers for retry/backoff that can be dropped into prod code. Avoid shipping credentialed secrets in repo; use env vars. Add LICENSE and Contributing note.
next_steps: Merge helper libraries behind feature flag, run cross-language smoke tests, add short screencast for onboarding, then announce in #sdk-channel and update developer quickstart page.
